intended_object: The germ at a node made by gluing two holomorphic germs f ∈ 𝒪_{X,p} and g ∈ 𝒪_{Y,q} that take the same value at their base points. It is the element (f, g) of the fibre product 𝒪_{X,p} ×_ℂ 𝒪_{Y,q}, i.e. of the node's local ring. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`nodeLocalRing I J p q` is defined as the subring of `𝒪_{X,p} × 𝒪_{Y,q}` cut out by the condition `eval (fst x) = eval (snd x)`. So the subring is the fibre product of the two maps that evaluate a germ at its base point.

`mk f g h` packages the pair `(f, g)` with the proof `h` that the two values agree. That proof is exactly the membership condition (`mem_nodeLocalRing` holds by `Iff.rfl`). This is the standard way to build an element of a fibre product from compatible components, and the lemmas `fst_mk` and `snd_mk` confirm that the two branch restrictions return `f` and `g`.

There are no missing or extra conditions, and no degenerate case where it goes wrong. The definition also already works for complex manifolds of any dimension, so it is not too narrow.

Mathlib's general counterpart would be the subtype constructor for `RingHom.eqLocus` (or an element of the pullback in `CommRingCat`), but Mathlib has no named declaration for this specific constructor. Since `mk` is a thin constructor, one could also call it a technical device. Still, it does exactly what its docstring says: it glues compatible branch germs into a germ at the node.
